sections.h2: Where are Emmet County deeds recorded?
sections.html:
Emmet County's Register of Deeds works from 200 Division Street, Suite 150, in Petoskey, MI 49770, and answers at 231-348-1761. Every deed for land in the county, from Harbor Springs to Pellston, ends up in this one office.

It handles more than 240 kinds of paper, including deeds, mortgages with their assignments and discharges, land contracts, leases, liens, probate orders, condominium documents and plats. The register also chairs the county plat board, which reviews new subdivisions.

Land records start in 1852. Images exist from that year forward, yet the name index only runs from 1922 on, with earlier years being added a little at a time. For older searches the county invites people in to use the index books at the counter.

sections.h2: What does Emmet County charge to record documents?
sections.html:
Recording starts at $30 per document, collected at the counter by cash or check only. The register's page supplies the remaining numbers.

Emmet County register fee schedule, taken from the county's posted fee list
ServiceFee
Entering and recording any document$30
Warranty deeds, land contracts, covenant deeds and similar$35
Document assigning or discharging more than one instrument$3 per instrument
Certification of a document$5
Tax certification, up to 5 descriptions$5
Each added description20 cents
Copies$1.00 a page in the office, $1.05 online

The $35 line applies to any deed carrying a warrant or covenant clause, and the $5 tax certification has to be added to that payment. By mail, write the check to the Emmet County Register of Deeds.

sections.h2: What makes an Emmet County filing bounce?
sections.html:
Staff measure every filing against Michigan's recording statutes and send back whatever misses. The county prints the rules with statute numbers, and these are the ones that trip people up most.

  • Signatures must be originals, with printed names beneath, and the notary's acknowledgment must carry the same names.
  • Leave 2.5 inches of blank space at the top of page one and half an inch around every other edge.
  • Use black ink in 10-point type or larger, on white paper weighing at least 20 pounds, between letter size and 8.5 by 14.
  • Show the drafter's name and address on any document signed in Michigan.
  • Print no more than the last four digits of a Social Security number.
  • One instrument covers one recordable event.
  • Court orders arrive certified with the clerk's seal, and a survivorship deed needs a certified death certificate already on record.

Include a return envelope. The office usually records a paper the day it arrives, keeps it one day and mails it back the next business day, unless the title company or lender gave other instructions.

sections.h2: How does Emmet County figure Michigan transfer tax?
sections.html:
The state tax is $3.75 per $500 of value (MCL 207.525) and the county tax is 55 cents per $500 where a county has fewer than two million residents (MCL 207.504). The full price has to be visible on the deed, or an affidavit of value must be attached.

Emmet County posts a transfer tax table, a list of exemptions and a state refund form among its downloads. The statutes load the tax on the seller (MCL 207.502 and 207.523).

A $315,700 home, which is the QuickFacts median for Emmet County, falls into 632 steps of $500. State tax is $2,370.00, county tax $347.60, together $2,717.60. A deed from a parent to a child, or from a grandparent to a grandchild, skips the state tax under MCL 207.526, provided the instrument says so.

sections.h2: Why does the recording order matter under Michigan law?
sections.html:
Michigan runs a race-notice system, and Emmet County's register explains it in a few words: a recorded deed puts every later buyer on notice, so papers count in the exact order they were first presented. First in time, first in line.

After a closing, the deed and the buyer's mortgage should reach the register without delay, because a gap lets a later filing jump the queue. Title companies know this and tend to record the same day. A private sale without one means delivering the deed yourself, or using one of the county's e-recording providers: CSC, EPN or Simplifile.

The county page carries a ROD Alert about outside companies that offer certified copies of a deed for $50 or more. Copies cost as little as $1 a page at the register, and the office asks residents to call 231-348-1761 before paying a third party.

sections.h2: Can you search Emmet County records without paying?
sections.html:
Yes, once you register for the county's free site. Searches run by liber and page, name or document type, and a low-resolution preview appears before you buy a copy by card at $1.05 a page. A companion service called Fraud Notify emails you whenever a document is recorded under your name.

Tax information lives in a separate property search on the county website, which takes a name, an address or a parcel number. Anyone buying or inheriting a house in the county should look at both.

sections.h2: What sets the Emmet County market apart from other counties?
sections.html:
Emmet County sits at the tip of the Lower Peninsula, with Lake Michigan to the west and the Straits of Mackinac to the north. It measures 882 square miles, but only 467 are land. Little Traverse Bay and the inland lakes account for the other 47%. Petoskey is both the county seat and its largest city. Harbor Springs is the second city, and the villages are Alanson, Pellston and part of Mackinaw City.

QuickFacts counts 15,190 households. Owners live in 77.0% of homes, a typical owned home is worth $315,700 and household income has a median of $78,112. About 28.5% of residents are 65 or older. The July 2025 estimate was 33,775 people in 22,395 housing units.

McLaren Northern Michigan Hospital in Petoskey employs about 950 people, and the Odawa Casino Resort in Resort Township is one of the county's major attractions. Moeller Aerospace Technology is in Harbor Springs, and Kilwins, the candy and ice cream company founded in 1947, is based in Petoskey.

sections.h2: What if the Emmet County house has back taxes?
sections.html:
Delinquent taxes are collected through the county treasurer's office, and a deed cannot be recorded without a tax certification from that office. The register accepts redemption payments during the redemption period. Once it ends, only the foreclosing unit can help.

A sale can clear the debt. The closer pays the balance out of the proceeds and then requests the certification the register needs, so get a payoff number from the treasurer before a closing date is picked.

faqs.q: What is the street address for the Emmet County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: 200 Division Street, Suite 150, Petoskey, MI 49770, phone 231-348-1761. Recording fees are paid in person by cash or check only.

faqs.q: How much is a warranty deed recording in Emmet County?
faqs.a: Thirty-five dollars. The base recording fee is $30, and warranty deeds, land contracts and other covenant-language deeds are listed at $35, with the $5 tax certification included in the payment.

faqs.q: Does Emmet County accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: Yes, through three providers: CSC, EPN and Simplifile. Contact one of them for guidance on sending a deed in electronically.

faqs.q: How old are Emmet County land records?
faqs.a: They start in 1852. Images are indexed from 1922 forward and earlier indexing continues, so some older searches mean a trip to the index books.

faqs.q: Does a deed signed in Michigan need witnesses?
faqs.a: No. Emmet County's register says witnesses are no longer required, though most documents still need a notary acknowledgment.
